# Insurance tariff lookup

A shared per-key query cache provides subscribe(key,options) -> unique observer
handle, unsubscribe(handle), online(boolean), focus(boolean), snapshot(key),
and dispose() of observer scopes. Queries retain status (pending/success/error),
fetchStatus (idle/fetching/paused), and data. queryFn receives a lazy signal
accessor. Each actual access records consumption; each fetch owns its controller
and completion. Completion is asynchronous; initial online entry is synchronous,
paused continuation resumes on a Promise turn. First start uses network mode;
continuation also needs focus. 'always' can run offline; 'offlineFirst' allows
first offline entry but retry can pause. Retries use explicit scheduler handles.
Multiple observers share one fetch. Unconsumed active work can finish into cache
after its view departs; consumed work is physically abortable. Cancellation
reverts previous query data/status and settles the originating attempt. Late
fulfillment cannot become a new attempt's data. Unknown unsubscribe is inert.
The component owns observer scope; the cache remains outside individual views.
Dependency versions and build/test configuration are outside the repair scope.

Embedding API: bind registers a native callable; Environment.call
provides newAttempt(key,number), abort(key,number), request(key,number, lazy-read
token, completion token), defer(callback token), schedule(callback token,delay).
The request host calls queryFn with an actual AbortSignal property. Reading it
invokes the native consumption closure synchronously; Promise settlement later
invokes the native completion with {ok,value}. All observer, retry, cancellation,
state and cache logic executes in the target language. No native JS Promise or
DOM claim is made. Native object identity binds query and attempt generations;
wire handles only identify injected callbacks. 
PHP cache and observer objects; lazy context getter and Closure waiter

<?php
class FetchAttempt {
 public $number,$previous,$options,$settled=false,$entered=false,$consumed=false,$retryCancelled=false,$failures=0,$queued=false;
 function __construct($number,$state,$options){$this->number=$number;$this->previous=$state;$this->options=$options;}
}
class CachedQuery {
 public $key,$state,$observers=[],$attempt=null,$consumed=false;
 function __construct($key,$data){$this->key=$key;$this->state=['status'=>$data!==null?'success':'pending','fetchStatus'=>'idle','data'=>$data];}
}
class Session {
 private $env,$cache=[],$handles=[],$online,$focused,$serial=0,$fetchSerial=0;
 function __construct($env,$initial){$this->env=$env;$this->online=$initial['online']??true;$this->focused=$initial['focused']??true;}
 function eligible($a){return $this->focused&&(($a->options['networkMode']??'online')==='always'||$this->online);}
 function active($q,$a){return $q->attempt===$a&&!$a->settled;}
 function cancel($q,$a){if($a->settled)return;$a->settled=true;$q->state=$a->previous;$q->state['fetchStatus']='idle';$this->env->call('abort',$q->key,$a->number);}
 function invoke($q,$a){$a->queued=false;if(!$this->active($q,$a))return;$a->entered=true;$a->consumed=false;$q->state['fetchStatus']='fetching';$q->consumed=false;
  $getter=$this->env->bind(function($_)use($q,$a){$a->consumed=true;$q->consumed=true;return null;});
  $done=$this->env->bind(function($value)use($q,$a){if(!$this->active($q,$a))return;if($value['ok']){$a->settled=true;$q->state=array_merge($q->state,['data'=>$value['value'],'status'=>'success','fetchStatus'=>'idle']);}
   elseif(!$a->retryCancelled&&$a->failures<($a->options['retry']??0)){$a->failures++;$retry=$this->env->bind(function($_)use($q,$a){if(!$this->active($q,$a))return;if($a->retryCancelled){$a->settled=true;$q->state['status']='error';$q->state['fetchStatus']='idle';return;}if($this->eligible($a))$this->invoke($q,$a);else $q->state['fetchStatus']='paused';});$this->env->call('schedule',$retry,$a->options['retryDelay']??10);}
   else{$a->settled=true;$q->state['status']='error';$q->state['fetchStatus']='idle';}return null;});$this->env->call('request',$q->key,$a->number,$getter,$done);
 }
 function resume($q){$a=$q->attempt;if($a&&$this->active($q,$a)&&$q->state['fetchStatus']==='paused'&&$this->eligible($a)&&!$a->queued){$a->queued=true;$token=$this->env->bind(function($_)use($q,$a){$a->queued=false;if(!$this->active($q,$a))return;if($a->failures&&$a->retryCancelled){$a->settled=true;$q->state['status']='error';$q->state['fetchStatus']='idle';return;}$this->invoke($q,$a);});$this->env->call('defer',$token);}}
 function subscribe($key,$options){if(!isset($this->cache[$key]))$this->cache[$key]=new CachedQuery($key,$options['initialData']??null);$q=$this->cache[$key];$handle=++$this->serial;$this->handles[$handle]=$q;$q->observers[$handle]=true;if($q->attempt&&!$q->attempt->settled){$q->attempt->retryCancelled=false;$this->resume($q);}else{$a=new FetchAttempt(++$this->fetchSerial,$q->state,$options);$q->attempt=$a;$this->env->call('newAttempt',$key,$a->number);if(($options['networkMode']??'online')!=='online'||$this->online)$this->invoke($q,$a);else $q->state['fetchStatus']='paused';}return $handle;}
 function unsubscribe($handle){$q=$this->handles[$handle]??null;if(!$q)return;unset($this->handles[$handle],$q->observers[$handle]);if(count($q->observers)===0){$a=$q->attempt;if($a&&!$a->settled){if($a->consumed)$this->cancel($q,$a);elseif(!$a->entered){$a->settled=true;$q->state=$a->previous;$q->state['fetchStatus']='idle';}else $a->retryCancelled=true;}}}
 function handle($name,$args){switch($name){case 'subscribe':return $this->subscribe(...$args);case 'unsubscribe':$this->unsubscribe($args[0]);return null;case 'snapshot':return $this->cache[$args[0]]->state;case 'dispose':foreach(array_keys($this->handles)as $h)$this->unsubscribe($h);return null;case 'online':$this->online=$args[0];break;case 'focus':$this->focused=$args[0];break;default:throw new Exception($name);}foreach($this->cache as $q)$this->resume($q);return null;}
}

checkpoints: Subscribe a fresh key in online mode while offline: create the observer and attempt, leave the query paused, and do not enter the query function or consume its signal.
Remove the final observer while that fresh attempt is still paused before first entry: the attempt must lose authority to start, including through an already-deferred continuation.
Reconnect and regain focus after departure: no request or lazy-signal access may occur for the abandoned attempt.
Subscribe again to the same cached key: create a new attempt that follows the normal online/focus rules; stale callbacks from the abandoned attempt must not affect it.

Verify remaining observers still retain shared work, entered unconsumed work may still complete into the cache, consumed work remains physically abortable, retries retain their documented scheduling behavior, and unknown unsubscribe remains inert.
Run the public PHP syntax check after any Action; it is required but does not establish business correctness.
forbidden_effects: Do not invoke the signal-consuming query function for the fresh online-mode attempt after its final observer departed while it was offline and before first entry.
Do not let reconnect behavior or a refetchOnReconnect setting restore authority to the abandoned attempt.
Do not treat every observer departure as cancellation: shared work with remaining observers and supported already-entered unconsumed work must retain their documented behavior.
Do not let a stale request completion or deferred callback publish data, errors, retries, or state into a later attempt.
Do not change public commands, observer handles, cache identity, native bindings, dependencies, or build/test configuration.
Do not edit tests or configuration; any Action is limited to product source.
lifecycle_identity: The cache and CachedQuery are persistent per-key owners outside individual observer views.
Each subscribe call owns a unique observer handle; only removal of the final observer triggers observerless-attempt policy.
Each FetchAttempt object and its attempt number identify one originating attempt; replacement attempts must remain isolated from old callbacks and completions.
The lazy signal accessor belongs to the request for its captured query and attempt; actual access records consumption for that work.
Deferred and scheduled callback tokens are delivery mechanisms, not authority to revive an attempt that has been settled or otherwise invalidated.

obligations.text: When a fresh online-mode query is subscribed while offline, it may remain paused without entering the query function.

If the final observer unsubscribes while that fresh attempt is paused and has never entered its query function, invalidate or settle that attempt so neither later reconnect nor an already-queued continuation can enter it with a live signal.
Apply the O2 protection independently of refetchOnReconnect; reconnect must not revive observerless, never-entered work.
Preserve per-key cache ownership and attempt isolation so a later subscription can start a new attempt while stale callbacks and completions from the abandoned attempt remain ineffective.

Preserve supported shared-query behavior: remaining observers keep shared work alive, already-entered unconsumed work may finish into cache after view departure, consumed work remains physically abortable, and cancellation restores previous state and settles the originating attempt.
Preserve network modes, focus gating, retry scheduling, asynchronous completion, public interfaces, dependencies, and build/test configuration; change product source only.

ordering_barriers: Final-observer departure must revoke the never-entered attempt before any reconnect/focus resume can call invoke or request.
A deferred resume callback must revalidate that its captured attempt is still active and authorized immediately before entering the query function.
Request completion must verify that its captured attempt is still the query's active unsettled attempt before changing cached state.
Attempt cancellation or invalidation must occur before replacement work can be affected by callbacks belonging to the old attempt.
Signal consumption is recorded only when the lazy accessor is actually read; merely creating an attempt, pausing it, or binding a getter is not consumption.

Keep one cache entry per key with shared observers and one current attempt, while preserving independent keys.
Keep synchronous eligible initial entry, asynchronous completion, Promise-turn paused continuation, and explicit retry scheduler handles.
Keep network-mode behavior: always may run offline, offlineFirst may enter initially offline but may pause on retry, and ordinary online mode pauses offline.
Keep focus gating for continuation.
Keep prior data/status restoration and originating-attempt settlement on cancellation.
Keep late-fulfillment isolation, unknown-unsubscribe inertness, and final scope disposal behavior.
Keep the documented distinction between observer scope and the longer-lived cache.
